gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Xebec's help center says Snap pass-through charging may not start at all with a charger above about 100 W. A 16-inch MacBook Pro ships with Apple's 140 W adapter, so on that laptop, which is the size Xebec's stacked setup is pitched at, the owner needs a separate 45–100 W charger. Xebec also says DisplayLink screens can show black video for Netflix, Disney+, Prime and YouTube TV.
standout_why: I opened Macworld's Duex Float 2 Pro review (cited in 4 chats) and our own Dealectric page. Macworld covers only the Duex: its 16-inch MacBook Pro fit, the 15 W charger for full brightness and the 65 W pass-back. It says nothing about Xebec. Our page lists Xebec only as 'USB-C, DisplayLink chip built in' and 'on the Stack-Up Mount ($99) over the lid bracket'. It does not mention the ~100 W pass-through ceiling, the DisplayLink protected-video problem, the one-mount, left-wing-only Stack-Up rule or the macOS 11+ floor. I did not open Wired, Fstoppers, itechguides, Mobile Pixels' Black Friday blog or Macworld's Mac roundup in this session, so a rival covering these points is possible but not checked.
decides: Confirms the Duex Float 2 Pro as the pick for 15–16-inch laptops. It drives the screen natively over DP Alt Mode USB-C (no DisplayLink, so no streaming black-out), and Macworld names the 16-inch MacBook Pro as its best fit. It also adds a caveat to the Xebec Snap + Stack-Up row: on a 16-inch MacBook Pro the bundled 140 W charger is above Xebec's ~100 W pass-through ceiling, protected streaming may go black on the stacked screen, and the Stack-Up Mount holds only one stacked screen (one per bracket, left wing only). That narrows Xebec to 13–14-inch laptops whose own chargers are 100 W or less, which is the size ChatGPT already steers it to, and now with a sourced reason.

findings.label: Pass-through charger wattage range
findings.value: 45–100 W for one screen, 55–100 W for two; 'Above roughly 100W the connection may not start at all'
findings.source_title: My pass through charging feature on my Snap is not working. What do I do? | Xebec Help Center
findings.note: Maker's help article, marked 'Updated a month ago'. It also says power software such as Dell Power Manager or Lenovo Vantage, and docking stations, can block pass-through.

findings.label: Charger in the box, 16-inch MacBook Pro
findings.value: 140 W USB-C Power Adapter (only adapter listed for the 16-inch)
findings.note: The 140 W adapter is above Xebec's ~100 W pass-through ceiling. The 14-inch ships with 70 W (M6, M5 Pro 15-core) or 96 W (M5 Pro 18-core, M5 Max), both inside Xebec's range.

findings.label: Protected streaming on DisplayLink screens
findings.value: Video stays black with audio playing for protected content (Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime, HBO, iTunes, YouTube TV, Udemy) while DisplayLink screens are connected
findings.source_title: My streaming services like Netflix and YouTube are not working when connected. How to fix? | Xebec Help Center
findings.note: Xebec's workarounds: disconnect all DisplayLink screens, switch browser, or turn off browser hardware acceleration. Xebec states the Snap screen has a DisplayLink chip (see the compatibility page). The Duex Float 2 Pro uses native DP Alt Mode, not DisplayLink.

findings.label: Stack-Up Mount limits
findings.value: One Stack-Up Mount per Snap Bracket; it attaches only to the left Bracket wing, in the closed position
findings.source_title: How do I connect my Stack-Up Mount? | Xebec Help Center
findings.note: So the setup gives one screen above the laptop, not two stacked. The page states no laptop-size limit for stacking.

findings.label: Supported laptops and OS floor
findings.value: Mac, Windows/PC, Chromebook and Linux laptops 13–17.5 in; 'not compatible with laptops unable to support Mac OS11+'; USB-A laptops need the free DisplayLink driver; free Surface adapters for Surface Pro
findings.source_title: What laptops does Xebec Snap work with? | Xebec Help Center
findings.note: One cable per screen, over USB-C or USB-A. A separate Xebec help listing names Surface Pro 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 as compatible (https://help.thexebec.com/en-US/articles/snap-products-100861).

findings.label: Bracket fit exclusions
findings.value: Ultra-thin laptops, thick laptops and laptops in protective cases may not hold the Snap Bracket; Xebec sends a Snap Bracket Adapter on request
findings.source_title: My Snap Bracket does not fit around my laptop. What do I do? | Xebec Help Center
findings.note: No lid-thickness range in mm and no laptop models are named.

findings.label: Best-fit laptop (named reviewer)
findings.value: Macworld (Simon Jary): 'a great fit for owners of the 16-inch MacBook Pro in particular'; mirrors the 16-inch display
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: Review dated 2025-12-16. The review does not cover 13- or 14-inch MacBooks. The four removable magnets go on the laptop lid, placed with a cardboard template; without them the laptop leans on the Float, which Jary says is less stable.

findings.label: Power and pass-through
findings.value: PD USB-C charger of 15 W or more for full brightness without flicker; up to 65 W passed back to the laptop when a wall charger is connected; Limited Power Mode on laptop power alone caps brightness at 80% (7.5 W, measured on the non-Pro Float 2)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: From the review, not the maker's page, which returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. The 65 W pass-back is below the 16-inch MacBook Pro's 140 W adapter, so that laptop would charge slower through the monitor (my inference).

findings.label: Devices
findings.value: MacBooks via USB-C; iPhone 15 or later 'due to the required USB-C connection'; HDMI-to-mini-HDMI cable included
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro review: Portable screen that floats above your MacBook | Macworld
findings.note: Macworld does not say whether a driver is needed.

findings.label: Connection by laptop port type
findings.value: USB-C with DP Alt Mode: one USB-C to C cable; USB-C without DP Alt Mode: USB-C to C cable plus HDMI cable; USB-A and HDMI only: USB-C to C cable with USB-A adapter plus HDMI cable
findings.note: The page covers the original Duex Float and does not name the Float 2 Pro. The Macworld review confirms USB-C plus a mini-HDMI option on the Float 2 Pro.
